tagline: Lighthouses, orchards, and a shoreline on both sides.
intro: The Door County Coastal Byway loops around the northern Door Peninsula, the thumb of land between Green Bay and Lake Michigan. One side of the loop follows the calmer bay shore and its harbour villages. The other follows the open Lake Michigan side, with limestone ledges and quieter coves.
It is a short byway by distance, so the day is set by how often you stop.
season: Summer for the villages, autumn for colour along the bluff.

moments.title: Peninsula State Park
moments.text: Wooded bluffs above Green Bay between Fish Creek and Ephraim.

moments.title: Ephraim
moments.text: A small harbour village on Eagle Harbor, on the bay side of the loop.

moments.title: Cana Island Lighthouse
moments.text: A lighthouse on a small island off the Lake Michigan shore, reached by a causeway.

moments.title: Cave Point County Park
moments.text: Wave-cut limestone ledges on the Lake Michigan side.

practical: Directions go to Sturgeon Bay, where the loop begins.
WisDOT now lists this road as a National Scenic Byway. The 2022 national dataset shown here records only its state designation.
